subproblems.title: Lusin's theorem (compact form) for measurable maps from ℝ^P into a second-countable space (reused accepted theorem; Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 1.17)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, and let Y be a second-countable topological space with a σ-algebra in which every open set is measurable. Let μ be any measure on ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) (Borel σ-algebra), let A ⊆ ℝ^P be a measurable set with μ(A) < ∞, let g : ℝ^P → Y be measurable, and let ε ∈ (0, ∞] be an extended nonnegative real with ε ≠ 0. Then there is a compact set K ⊆ A with μ(A ∖ K) < ε such that g is continuous on K (ContinuousOn g K).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) {Y : Type} [TopologicalSpace Y] [SecondCountableTopology Y] [MeasurableSpace Y] [OpensMeasurableSpace Y] (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (A : Set (Euclid P)) (g : Euclid P → Y) (ε : ℝ≥0∞), Measurable g → MeasurableSet A → μ A ≠ ∞ → ε ≠ 0 → ∃ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K ∧ K ⊆ A ∧ μ (A \ K) < ε ∧ ContinuousOn g K
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: this is the accepted DAG theorem `dor_ims_lusin_measurable_continuousOn` (node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.imrep_mass_and_support-a1.lusin_covector-a1.lusin_measurable-a1, accepted candidate e4172a7b), reused with its byte-identical frozen type. It is Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 1.17, used in Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6, for the closed set F of (4); the selected node already depends on it. Its accepted parent-supplied proof is reproduced verbatim.

Hypotheses: P ∈ ℕ. Y is a second-countable topological space with a σ-algebra in which every open set is measurable. μ is any measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra). A ⊆ ℝ^P is measurable with μ(A) < ∞. g : ℝ^P → Y is measurable. ε ∈ [0, ∞] with ε ≠ 0.
1. (Inner regularity inside A.) Let ν := μ.restrict A, so ν(B) = μ(B ∩ A) for measurable B.
 ν is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P, since ν(ℝ^P) = μ(A) < ∞. A finite measure is locally finite, and ℝ^P is a σ-compact (indeed proper) metric space, so ν is regular (Mathlib instance Regular.of_sigmaCompactSpace_of_isLocallyFiniteMeasure). Hence ν is inner regular by compact sets on measurable sets of finite measure (InnerRegularCompactLTTop). (Alternatively, Ulam's theorem: finite Borel measures on the Polish space ℝ^P are tight.)
 Consequently (MeasurableSet.exists_isCompact_sdiff_lt), for every measurable B ⊆ A and every η ∈ (0, ∞] there is a compact C ⊆ B with ν(B ∖ C) < η. C is compact in a Hausdorff space, hence closed and measurable. So B ∖ C is measurable and contained in A, and ν(B ∖ C) = μ((B ∖ C) ∩ A) = μ(B ∖ C). Thus μ(B ∖ C) < η.
2. (Countable basis.) Since Y is second countable, fix a countable basis 𝓑 of its topology. Y is nonempty (it contains g(0)) and ⋃𝓑 = Y, so 𝓑 is nonempty. Enumerate it as 𝓑 = {O_k : k ∈ ℕ}, with repetitions allowed. Each O_k is open, hence measurable in Y. Since g is measurable, S_k := g^{−1}(O_k) is a measurable subset of ℝ^P.
3. (Weights.) Choose η_k ∈ (0, ∞) for k ∈ ℕ with Σ_k η_k < ε. For example, put δ := min(ε, 1) ∈ (0, 1] and η_k := δ·2^{−k−2}; then Σ_k η_k = δ/2 < δ ≤ ε. (In Mathlib: ENNReal.exists_pos_sum_of_countable'.)
4. (Compact pieces.) Fix k. The sets A ∩ S_k and A ∖ S_k are measurable subsets of A. By step 1 with η = η_k/2 > 0, choose compact sets C_k ⊆ A ∩ S_k and D_k ⊆ A ∖ S_k with
 μ((A ∩ S_k) ∖ C_k) < η_k/2 and μ((A ∖ S_k) ∖ D_k) < η_k/2.
 Put E_k := C_k ∪ D_k, a compact subset of A. Let x ∈ A ∖ E_k. If g(x) ∈ O_k, then x ∈ (A ∩ S_k) ∖ C_k; otherwise x ∈ (A ∖ S_k) ∖ D_k. Hence A ∖ E_k ⊆ ((A ∩ S_k) ∖ C_k) ∪ ((A ∖ S_k) ∖ D_k), and subadditivity gives μ(A ∖ E_k) < η_k/2 + η_k/2 = η_k.
5. (The compact set.) Let K := ⋂_k E_k.
 Each E_k is compact in the Hausdorff space ℝ^P, hence closed, so K is closed. K lies in the compact set E_0, so K is compact, being a closed subset of a compact set. Also K ⊆ E_0 ⊆ A.
 Since A ∖ K = ⋃_k (A ∖ E_k), countable subadditivity and steps 3–4 give μ(A ∖ K) ≤ Σ_k μ(A ∖ E_k) ≤ Σ_k η_k < ε.
6. (Continuity.) Fix k and x ∈ K, so x ∈ E_k = C_k ∪ D_k.
 - If x ∉ D_k, then x ∈ C_k ⊆ A ∩ S_k, so g(x) ∈ O_k.
 - If g(x) ∈ O_k, then x ∈ S_k, so x ∉ D_k because D_k ⊆ A ∖ S_k.
 Hence K ∩ g^{−1}(O_k) = K ∩ (ℝ^P ∖ D_k). D_k is compact, hence closed, so ℝ^P ∖ D_k is open. Therefore the preimage of O_k under the restriction g|_K : K → Y is open in the subspace topology of K.
 Every open subset of Y is a union of sets O_k, so its preimage under g|_K is a union of open subsets of K, hence open (IsTopologicalBasis.continuous_iff). Therefore g|_K is continuous, i.e. ContinuousOn g K (continuousOn_iff_continuous_restrict).
 Together with step 5, K is a compact subset of A with μ(A ∖ K) < ε on which g is continuous. ∎
proof_key_steps: ν = μ⌞A is finite, so it is regular on ℝ^P (a σ-compact metric space) and hence inner regular by compacts: each measurable B ⊆ A contains a compact C with μ(B ∖ C) = ν(B ∖ C) < η.
Enumerate a countable basis (O_k)_{k∈ℕ} of Y; each S_k = g⁻¹(O_k) is measurable.
Choose positive weights η_k with Σ η_k < ε, e.g. min(ε,1)·2^{−k−2}.
Choose compact C_k ⊆ A ∩ S_k and D_k ⊆ A ∖ S_k with defects < η_k/2; E_k = C_k ∪ D_k ⊆ A has μ(A ∖ E_k) < η_k.
K = ⋂_k E_k is closed inside the compact E_0, hence compact; K ⊆ A and μ(A ∖ K) ≤ Σ_k μ(A ∖ E_k) < ε.
For x ∈ K, g(x) ∈ O_k ⇔ x ∉ D_k, so (g|_K)⁻¹(O_k) = K ∩ D_kᶜ is open in K and g is continuous on K.

subproblems.title: Lusin's theorem for an a.e. strongly measurable map, keeping an a.e. property (parent steps 1–2; the closed set F of Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6, (4))
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let Y be a pseudo-metrizable, second-countable topological space. Let μ be a measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra), A ⊆ ℝ^P a Borel set with μ(A) < ∞, f : ℝ^P → Y a map that is almost everywhere strongly measurable with respect to μ⌞A, and p a property of points of ℝ^P that holds μ⌞A-almost everywhere. Then for every η ∈ (0, ∞] (η ≠ 0) there is a compact set K ⊆ A with μ(A ∖ K) < η such that p(x) holds for every x ∈ K and f is continuous on K.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) {Y : Type} [TopologicalSpace Y] [TopologicalSpace.PseudoMetrizableSpace Y] [SecondCountableTopology Y] (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (A : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → Y) (p : Euclid P → Prop), MeasurableSet A → μ A ≠ ∞ → AEStronglyMeasurable f (μ.restrict A) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict A), p x) → ∀ η : ℝ≥0∞, η ≠ 0 → ∃ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K ∧ K ⊆ A ∧ μ (A \ K) < η ∧ (∀ x ∈ K, p x) ∧ ContinuousOn f K
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 1–2 (a Borel set of good points; Lusin), which produce the closed set F of Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6 “⇐”, (4) (chapter-03.txt lines 168–172). The parent applies it with μ := Hⁿ, A := M, Y := L(ℝ^P) with the operator norm, f(x) := p_{Q(x)} and p(x) := “M has approximate tangent space Q(x) at x”.

1. A Borel representative. Since f is a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞A, there is a strongly measurable g : ℝ^P → Y with f = g μ⌞A-almost everywhere (Mathlib `AEStronglyMeasurable.mk`, `stronglyMeasurable_mk`, `ae_eq_mk`). Give Y its Borel σ-algebra, so every open subset of Y is measurable. Y is pseudo-metrizable, so the strongly measurable map g (a pointwise limit of simple functions) is measurable (Mathlib `StronglyMeasurable.measurable`).
2. A Borel set of good points. Let Z := {x ∈ ℝ^P : f(x) ≠ g(x) or p(x) fails}. Both {f ≠ g} and {x : p(x) fails} are μ⌞A-null, so μ⌞A(Z) = 0. Since A is measurable, μ⌞A(Z) = μ(Z ∩ A) (Mathlib `Measure.restrict_apply'`), so μ(Z ∩ A) = 0. Choose a measurable N ⊇ Z ∩ A with μ(N) = 0 (Mathlib `exists_measurable_superset_of_null`) and put A₁ := A ∖ N. Then A₁ is measurable and μ(A₁) ≤ μ(A) < ∞. Every x ∈ A₁ satisfies f(x) = g(x) and p(x): x ∈ A and x ∉ N ⊇ Z ∩ A, so x ∉ Z.
3. Lusin. Apply the sibling lusin (Lusin's theorem, compact form) to the measure μ, the measurable set A₁ (μ(A₁) < ∞), the measurable map g : ℝ^P → Y (Y is second countable and its open sets are measurable) and the tolerance η ≠ 0. This gives a compact K ⊆ A₁ with μ(A₁ ∖ K) < η such that g is continuous on K.
4. Verification. K is compact and K ⊆ A₁ ⊆ A. Every x ∈ K lies in A₁, so p(x) holds and f(x) = g(x). Hence f and g agree on K, and f is continuous on K because g is (Mathlib `ContinuousOn.congr`). Finally A ∖ K ⊆ N ∪ (A₁ ∖ K): if x ∈ A ∖ K and x ∉ N, then x ∈ A₁ ∖ K. By subadditivity, μ(A ∖ K) ≤ μ(N) + μ(A₁ ∖ K) = 0 + μ(A₁ ∖ K) < η. ∎
proof_key_steps: Replace f by a strongly measurable, hence Borel measurable, representative g with f = g μ⌞A-a.e. (Y with its Borel σ-algebra).
The bad set Z = {f ≠ g} ∪ {¬p} has μ(Z ∩ A) = 0. A measurable null hull N gives A₁ := A ∖ N of full measure, on which f = g and p holds.
Lusin (sibling lusin) for g on A₁ with tolerance η: compact K ⊆ A₁ with μ(A₁ ∖ K) < η and g continuous on K.
f = g on K, so f is continuous on K; p holds on K; μ(A ∖ K) ≤ μ(N) + μ(A₁ ∖ K) < η.

subproblems.title: Upper semicontinuity of closed-ball mass: {y : s ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y))} is closed for a finite measure (parent step 4(i))
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, μ a finite measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra), ρ ∈ ℝ and s ∈ [0, ∞]. Then the set {y ∈ ℝ^P : s ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y))} is closed, where B̄_ρ(y) = {z : |z − y| ≤ ρ} is the closed ball.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (ρ : ℝ) (s : ℝ≥0∞), IsClosed {y : Euclid P | s ≤ μ (closedBall y ρ)}
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 4(i). Closedness of the sets A_k there replaces the measurability of Simon's functions f_k (Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6 “⇐”, (7)–(8)).

1. Reduction. ℝ^P is a metric space, hence a sequential space, so it suffices to show that the set is sequentially closed. Let (y_i)_{i∈ℕ} satisfy s ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y_i)) for every i and y_i → y; we prove s ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y)).
2. Complements. Put U := ℝ^P ∖ B̄_ρ(y) and U_i := ℝ^P ∖ B̄_ρ(y_i). Closed balls are closed, so U and the U_i are open, hence Borel.
3. Pointwise liminf bound. For every z ∈ ℝ^P, 1_U(z) ≤ liminf_i 1_{U_i}(z). If z ∉ U, the left side is 0. If z ∈ U, then |z − y| > ρ. Since |z − y_i| → |z − y| (continuity of the distance), |z − y_i| > ρ for all sufficiently large i, i.e. z ∈ U_i eventually. So 1_{U_i}(z) = 1 for all large i, and the liminf equals 1.
4. Fatou. The functions 1_{U_i} are measurable and nonnegative. By Fatou's lemma (Mathlib `lintegral_liminf_le`) and step 3, μ(U) = ∫ 1_U dμ ≤ ∫ liminf_i 1_{U_i} dμ ≤ liminf_i ∫ 1_{U_i} dμ = liminf_i μ(U_i).
5. Bounding μ(U_i). Since μ is finite and B̄_ρ(y_i) is measurable, μ(U_i) = μ(ℝ^P) − μ(B̄_ρ(y_i)) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) − s. Here truncated subtraction on [0, ∞] is antitone in the subtracted argument, and s ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y_i)). Every term is bounded by μ(ℝ^P) − s, so liminf_i μ(U_i) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) − s, and by step 4, μ(U) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) − s.
6. Conclusion. s ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y_0)) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) < ∞. As μ is finite and B̄_ρ(y) is measurable, μ(B̄_ρ(y)) = μ(ℝ^P) − μ(U) ≥ μ(ℝ^P) − (μ(ℝ^P) − s) = s. The last equality uses s ≤ μ(ℝ^P) < ∞. Hence y belongs to the set, which is therefore closed. ∎
proof_key_steps: Sequential closedness suffices in the metric space ℝ^P: take y_i → y with s ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y_i)).
The open complements satisfy 1_U ≤ liminf 1_{U_i} pointwise, where U = ℝ^P ∖ B̄_ρ(y) and U_i = ℝ^P ∖ B̄_ρ(y_i).
Fatou: μ(U) ≤ liminf μ(U_i) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) − s.
Finite measure: μ(B̄_ρ(y)) = μ(ℝ^P) − μ(U) ≥ s, using s ≤ μ(ℝ^P).

subproblems.title: Lower semicontinuity of cone mass along a continuous plane field: {x ∈ F : μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ s} is closed (parent step 4(ii))
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, μ any measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra), and F ⊆ ℝ^P a closed set. Let Q : ℝ^P → linear subspaces of ℝ^P be such that x ↦ p_{Q(x)} (orthogonal projection onto Q(x), an element of L(ℝ^P) with the operator norm) is continuous on F. Let ρ ∈ ℝ and s ∈ [0, ∞]. For x ∈ ℝ^P put X(x) := {z : 2|p_{Q(x)}(z − x)| < |z − x|} and B_ρ(x) := {z : |z − x| < ρ}. Then the set {x : x ∈ F and μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ s} is closed.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (F : Set (Euclid P)) (Q : Euclid P → Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (ρ : ℝ) (s : ℝ≥0∞), IsClosed F → ContinuousOn (fun x => (Q x).starProjection) F → IsClosed {x | x ∈ F ∧ μ ({z | 2 * ‖(Q x).starProjection (z - x)‖ < ‖z - x‖} ∩ ball x ρ) ≤ s}
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 4(ii). Closedness of the sets C_k there replaces the measurability of Simon's functions q_k (Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6 “⇐”, (7)–(8)). For w ∈ ℝ^P write L_w := p_{Q(w)} and S(w) := X(w) ∩ B_ρ(w).

1. Reduction. ℝ^P is a metric space, so it suffices to prove sequential closedness. Let x_i → x with x_i ∈ F and μ(S(x_i)) ≤ s for all i ∈ ℕ. Since F is closed, x ∈ F. It remains to show μ(S(x)) ≤ s.
2. Openness. For each w, the maps z ↦ 2|L_w(z − w)| and z ↦ |z − w| are continuous (L_w is a continuous linear map), so X(w) = {z : 2|L_w(z − w)| < |z − w|} is open. B_ρ(w) is open. Hence every S(w) is open, in particular Borel.
3. Convergence of the projections. The x_i lie in F and converge to x ∈ F, and w ↦ L_w is continuous on F, so ‖L_{x_i} − L_x‖ → 0 in the operator norm.
4. Pointwise liminf bound. Fix z ∈ S(x). We have L_{x_i}(z − x_i) − L_x(z − x) = (L_{x_i} − L_x)(z − x_i) + L_x(x − x_i). Hence |L_{x_i}(z − x_i) − L_x(z − x)| ≤ ‖L_{x_i} − L_x‖·|z − x_i| + ‖L_x‖·|x − x_i| → 0, because ‖L_{x_i} − L_x‖ → 0, |z − x_i| → |z − x| stays bounded, ‖L_x‖ ≤ 1 is fixed and |x − x_i| → 0. Also |z − x_i| → |z − x|. So 2|L_{x_i}(z − x_i)| − |z − x_i| → 2|L_x(z − x)| − |z − x| < 0 and |z − x_i| → |z − x| < ρ. For all sufficiently large i, therefore, 2|L_{x_i}(z − x_i)| < |z − x_i| and |z − x_i| < ρ, i.e. z ∈ S(x_i). So 1_{S(x_i)}(z) = 1 for all large i, and liminf_i 1_{S(x_i)}(z) = 1 = 1_{S(x)}(z). For z ∉ S(x), trivially 1_{S(x)}(z) = 0 ≤ liminf_i 1_{S(x_i)}(z). Thus 1_{S(x)} ≤ liminf_i 1_{S(x_i)} pointwise.
5. Fatou. The functions 1_{S(x_i)} are measurable (step 2) and nonnegative. Fatou's lemma (Mathlib `lintegral_liminf_le`) gives μ(S(x)) = ∫ 1_{S(x)} dμ ≤ ∫ liminf_i 1_{S(x_i)} dμ ≤ liminf_i ∫ 1_{S(x_i)} dμ = liminf_i μ(S(x_i)) ≤ s, the last step because every term is ≤ s. Hence x belongs to the set, which is therefore closed. ∎
proof_key_steps: Sequential closedness: x_i ∈ F, x_i → x, μ(S(x_i)) ≤ s; x ∈ F since F is closed.
Each S(w) = X(w) ∩ B_ρ(w) is open, hence Borel.
Continuity of w ↦ p_{Q(w)} on F gives operator-norm convergence, so every z ∈ S(x) lies in S(x_i) for all large i: 1_{S(x)} ≤ liminf 1_{S(x_i)}.
Fatou: μ(S(x)) ≤ liminf μ(S(x_i)) ≤ s.

subproblems.title: Egoroff-type uniformization of eventually-true closed conditions on a set of finite measure (parent steps 4(iii)–5)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra), F ⊆ ℝ^P a Borel set with μ(F) < ∞, and (T_ρ)_{ρ∈ℝ} a family of subsets of ℝ^P. Suppose T_ρ is closed for every ρ > 0, and every x ∈ F lies in T_ρ for all sufficiently small ρ > 0, i.e. there is r > 0 with x ∈ T_ρ for all ρ ∈ (0, r) (Lean: ∀ᶠ ρ in 𝓝[>] 0, x ∈ T ρ). Then for every η ∈ (0, ∞] (η ≠ 0) there are E ⊆ F and δ > 0 such that μ(F ∖ E) < η and x ∈ T_ρ for all x ∈ E and all ρ ∈ (0, δ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (F : Set (Euclid P)) (T : ℝ → Set (Euclid P)), MeasurableSet F → μ F ≠ ∞ → (∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → IsClosed (T ρ)) → (∀ x ∈ F, ∀ᶠ ρ in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), x ∈ T ρ) → ∀ η : ℝ≥0∞, η ≠ 0 → ∃ (E : Set (Euclid P)) (δ : ℝ), E ⊆ F ∧ 0 < δ ∧ μ (F \ E) < η ∧ ∀ x ∈ E, ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ < δ → x ∈ T ρ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 4(iii) and 5 (the increasing closed sets G_k and the Egoroff step). This is Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6 “⇐”, (7)–(9), with Egoroff's theorem (8) carried out on sets. The parent applies it with F := the compact set produced by Lusin and T_ρ := A_ρ ∩ C_ρ, the set of points satisfying the lower-density and cone bounds at radius ρ.

1. The sets G_k. For k ∈ ℕ let δ_k := 1/(k + 1) > 0 and G_k := F ∩ ⋂_{ρ ∈ (0, δ_k)} T_ρ. Every ρ in the intersection is positive, so ⋂_{ρ ∈ (0, δ_k)} T_ρ is an intersection of closed sets, hence closed. Since F is Borel, G_k is Borel.
2. Monotonicity. δ_{k+1} < δ_k, so (0, δ_{k+1}) ⊆ (0, δ_k) and therefore G_k ⊆ G_{k+1}: a point of F lying in T_ρ for all ρ ∈ (0, δ_k) lies in T_ρ for all ρ ∈ (0, δ_{k+1}).
3. Exhaustion. ⋃_k G_k = F. Clearly G_k ⊆ F. Conversely let x ∈ F. The sets (0, r), r > 0, form a basis of the filter 𝓝[>] 0, so the hypothesis gives r > 0 with x ∈ T_ρ for all ρ ∈ (0, r). By the Archimedean property choose k with 1/(k + 1) < r. Every ρ ∈ (0, δ_k) satisfies ρ < r, so x ∈ T_ρ; hence x ∈ G_k.
4. Continuity from above. The Borel sets D_k := F ∖ G_k decrease in k (step 2), ⋂_k D_k = F ∖ ⋃_k G_k = ∅ (step 3), and μ(D_0) ≤ μ(F) < ∞. By continuity of measure from above (Mathlib `tendsto_measure_iInter_atTop`), μ(F ∖ G_k) → μ(∅) = 0 as k → ∞.
5. Choice of E and δ. Since η > 0, step 4 gives k with μ(F ∖ G_k) < η. Put E := G_k ⊆ F and δ := δ_k > 0. If x ∈ E and 0 < ρ < δ, then x ∈ ⋂_{ρ' ∈ (0, δ_k)} T_ρ', so x ∈ T_ρ. ∎
proof_key_steps: G_k := F ∩ ⋂_{0<ρ<1/(k+1)} T_ρ is Borel (F Borel, intersection of closed sets).
G_k increases with k and ⋃_k G_k = F, by the eventual membership hypothesis and the Archimedean property.
Continuity from above for F ∖ G_k ↓ ∅ with μ(F) < ∞: μ(F ∖ G_k) → 0.
Choose k with μ(F ∖ G_k) < η; E := G_k, δ := 1/(k+1).
